proposal.name: Exponential lower bounds for Zadeh’s pivot rule
proposal.description:
## Motivation

The simplex method repeatedly replaces a basic variable by an improving nonbasic variable. A **pivot rule** specifies which improvement to make. Zadeh’s **least-entered rule** selects an improving variable that has entered the basis least often; equal counts require a separate tie rule. The paper establishes an exponential worst case for a specific strategy-dependent tie rule, alongside corresponding results for games and decision processes. It does not establish an exponential lower bound for every possible resolution of equal counts. [Primary paper](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-022-01848-x).

## Setting

The model fixes the paper’s finite two-centre counter, denoted $S_n$, with $n>0$ levels and terminal vertex $t$. A **positional strategy** assigns a successor at each controlled vertex. Infinite play is evaluated by the highest priority recurring infinitely often. Source indices start at one; the implementation uses zero-based level indices. Missing top-level centres are excluded by the vertex type.

A **Markov decision process** replaces each cycle centre by a random choice. Its probabilities are $\varepsilon$ to the upper selection vertex and $(1-\varepsilon)/2$ to each of two cycle vertices. The explicit parameters satisfy $N\ge7n$ and $0<\varepsilon<N^{-(2n+11)}$. The terminal value is zero. Deterministic reward vertices are retained as one-action decision vertices; eliminating them produces the same continuation equation. A generated occupancy linear program places one unit of input flow at every nonterminal decision vertex.

## Formalization targets

The goal combines the three conclusions for the constructed instances and the fixed tie rule:

$$T_{\mathrm{PG}}\ge2^n,\qquad T_{\mathrm{MDP}}\ge2^n,\qquad T_{\mathrm{LP}}\ge2^n.$$

Each component includes existence of a complete legal execution and the lower bound for every complete execution admitted by the rule. A complete execution ends only when no improving choice remains. Counting begins with zero occurrences, and a switch increments only its selected edge or entering variable. $T$ counts switches or pivots; the initial configuration is an additional displayed state.

The milestones cover finite size, priority valuation, the sink property, the tie ordering, canonical-state coverage, stochastic validity, and preservation of each switch by the generated linear program. The goal is not duplicated as a milestone. The canonical-state target requires a run to visit a strategy representing every integer from zero through $2^n-1$; it does not assume the lower bound in a hypothesis.

## Significance

The requested work is formal verification of a published lower-bound construction. Completing the mission would connect a concrete game, an exact rational stochastic model, and actual ratio-test simplex pivots. These are separately inspectable objects. Shared definitions can also support formal studies of other history-dependent pivot rules. The existence of open theorem targets in this package does not constitute a proof of those targets.

## Difficulty

Least-entered counts must be tracked throughout intermediate states. The tie rule depends on the current strategy, rather than a fixed ordering of variable names. The initial exceptional choice must also be preserved. The stochastic model has its own canonical-strategy convention, and policy improvement must correspond to an actual feasible simplex pivot. A proof that only follows the binary numbers without checking intervening choices would leave the principal obligations unresolved.

## Formalization scope

All graph, probability, reward and linear-program coefficients are explicit definitions. The LP basis matrix must have nonzero determinant, every pivot must satisfy the ratio test, and all visited MDP policies must have nonsingular sink-normalized Bellman equations. There is no assumed iteration count, abstract progress certificate, or lower-bound field in the data.

The source counter repeats priorities. Its valuation is therefore represented by priority multiplicities, with equal multiplicity vectors identified, following [Avis and Friedmann, Section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1305.3944v1). An integer-radix encoding realizes that finite lexicographic order; its equivalence is an explicit milestone. The transition direction used in the seven-class tie rule is concretely determined by comparing the current values of $b_2$ and $g_1$. Agreement with the source’s phase convention must be checked alongside canonical coverage. The rewards follow the labelled stochastic construction in Figure 5, retaining the high reward at deterministic $h$ vertices. These conventions are part of the draft audit.

## Selected references

- Yann Disser, Oliver Friedmann and Alexander V. Hopp, *An exponential lower bound for Zadeh’s pivot rule*, Mathematical Programming 199 (2023), 865–936. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-022-01848-x); [full version](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01074v2).
- David Avis and Oliver Friedmann, *An exponential lower bound for Cunningham’s rule*, Mathematical Programming 161 (2017), 271–305. [Priority-multiplicity valuation, Section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/1305.3944v1).
- Yann Disser and Alexander V. Hopp, *On Friedmann’s Subexponential Lower Bound for Zadeh’s Pivot Rule*, IPCO 2019. [Correction of the original 2011 construction](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-17953-3_13).

items.definition_title: Finite parity games and deterministic strategy improvement
items.definition:
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Prod
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Lattice.Fold
import Mathlib.Order.ConditionallyCompleteLattice.Basic
import Mathlib.Logic.Function.Iterate

set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
Finite parity games and the Vöge–Jurdziński valuation, as in Friedmann,
LMCS 2011, §§2–4. `false` denotes player 0. Functions representing strategies
are ignored at the other player's vertices. Definitions contain no open proofs.
-/
namespace FriedmannParity

structure Game (V : Type) where
  owner : V → Bool
  priority : V → ℕ
  edge : V → V → Prop

variable {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

def WellFormed (G : Game V) : Prop :=
  (∀ v, ∃ w, G.edge v w) ∧ Function.Injective G.priority

def Legal (G : Game V) (player : Bool) (σ : V → V) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, G.owner v = player → G.edge v (σ v)

def play (G : Game V) (σ τ : V → V) (v : V) : ℕ → V :=
  fun t => (fun w => if G.owner w = false then σ w else τ w)^[t] v

noncomputable def recurring (π : ℕ → V) : Finset V := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter (fun v => ∀ t, ∃ k, t ≤ k ∧ π k = v)

structure Valuation (V : Type) where
  cyclePriority : ℕ
  path : Finset V
  length : ℕ
  deriving DecidableEq

/- The finite orbit always has a recurring vertex. Thus `sup` and the least index have
their ordinary intended meanings on finite games; the valuation milestone makes
this obligation explicit. Empty V has no starting vertex. -/
noncomputable def playValue (G : Game V) (σ τ : V → V) (v : V) : Valuation V := by
  classical
  let π := play G σ τ v
  let p := (recurring π).sup G.priority
  let w := if h : ∃ w, w ∈ recurring π ∧ G.priority w = p
    then Classical.choose h else v
  let k := if h : ∃ k : ℕ, π k = w then Nat.find h else 0
  exact ⟨p, ((Finset.range k).image π).filter (fun w => p < G.priority w), k⟩

def reward (p : ℕ) : ℤ := if p % 2 = 0 then (p : ℤ) else -(p : ℤ)

def SetLT (G : Game V) (A B : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∃ w, w ∈ (A \ B) ∪ (B \ A) ∧
    (∀ u ∈ (A \ B) ∪ (B \ A), G.priority u ≤ G.priority w) ∧
    ((G.priority w % 2 = 0 ∧ w ∈ B) ∨ (G.priority w % 2 = 1 ∧ w ∈ A))

def ValueLT (G : Game V) (a b : Valuation V) : Prop :=
  reward a.cyclePriority < reward b.cyclePriority ∨
  (a.cyclePriority = b.cyclePriority ∧ SetLT G a.path b.path) ∨
  (a.cyclePriority = b.cyclePriority ∧ a.path = b.path ∧
    ((a.cyclePriority % 2 = 1 ∧ a.length < b.length) ∨
      (a.cyclePriority % 2 = 0 ∧ b.length < a.length)))

def ValueLE (G : Game V) (a b : Valuation V) : Prop := a = b ∨ ValueLT G a b

def IsMinimum (G : Game V) (σ : V → V) (v : V) (a : Valuation V) : Prop :=
  (∃ τ, Legal G true τ ∧ playValue G σ τ v = a) ∧
  ∀ τ, Legal G true τ → ValueLE G a (playValue G σ τ v)

/- A constrained minimum of actual legal counterstrategy valuations, never an
arbitrary valuation parameter. The fallback is irrelevant once existence is
proved for the finite, total, injective-priority model. -/
noncomputable def value (G : Game V) (σ : V → V) (v : V) : Valuation V :=
  by
    classical
    exact if h : ∃ a, IsMinimum G σ v a then Classical.choose h else ⟨0, ∅, 0⟩

def OptimalCounterstrategy (G : Game V) (σ τ : V → V) : Prop :=
  Legal G true τ ∧ ∀ v τ', Legal G true τ' →
    ValueLE G (playValue G σ τ v) (playValue G σ τ' v)

def Improving (G : Game V) (σ : V → V) (v w : V) : Prop :=
  G.owner v = false ∧ G.edge v w ∧
    ValueLT G (value G σ (σ v)) (value G σ w)

def Improvable (G : Game V) (σ : V → V) : Prop := ∃ v w, Improving G σ v w

def Allowed (G : Game V) (σ σ' : V → V) : Prop :=
  Legal G false σ' ∧ ∀ v, G.owner v = false →
    ValueLE G (value G σ (σ v)) (value G σ (σ' v))

def Improvement (G : Game V) (σ σ' : V → V) : Prop :=
  Allowed G σ σ' ∧
    (Improvable G σ → ∃ v, G.owner v = false ∧
      ValueLT G (value G σ (σ v)) (value G σ (σ' v)))

def LocalStep (G : Game V) (σ σ' : V → V) : Prop :=
  Improvement G σ σ' ∧ ∀ v w, G.owner v = false → G.edge v w →
    ValueLE G (value G σ w) (value G σ (σ' v))

def GlobalStep (G : Game V) (σ σ' : V → V) : Prop :=
  Improvement G σ σ' ∧ ∀ ρ, Allowed G σ ρ → ∀ v,
    ValueLE G (value G ρ v) (value G σ' v)

def CompleteRun (G : Game V) (step : (V → V) → (V → V) → Prop)
    (ι : V → V) (T : ℕ) (run : ℕ → (V → V)) : Prop :=
  run 0 = ι ∧ (∀ t, t ≤ T → Legal G false (run t)) ∧
    (∀ t, t < T → Improvable G (run t) ∧ step (run t) (run (t + 1))) ∧
    ¬ Improvable G (run T)

noncomputable def edgeCount (G : Game V) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter (fun e : V × V => G.edge e.1 e.2)).card

def HardInstance (G : Game V) (ι : V → V)
    (step : (V → V) → (V → V) → Prop) (iterations : ℕ) : Prop :=
  WellFormed G ∧ Legal G false ι ∧
    (∃ T run, CompleteRun G step ι T run) ∧
    ∀ T run, CompleteRun G step ι T run → iterations ≤ T

/- Both families, including their size bound, are conclusions to be proved.
No field or hypothesis supplies a long execution. The constant is uniform in n.
Size is edges, as in the source, rather than vertices or numeric bit length. -/
def ExponentialLocal : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ G : Game (Fin N), ∃ ι : Fin N → Fin N,
      edgeCount G ≤ C * n ∧
      (∀ v, G.priority v ≤ C * n) ∧ HardInstance G ι (LocalStep G) (2 ^ n)

def ExponentialGlobal : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ G : Game (Fin N), ∃ ι : Fin N → Fin N,
      edgeCount G ≤ C * n ∧
      (∀ v, G.priority v ≤ C * n) ∧ HardInstance G ι (GlobalStep G) (2 ^ n)

def Binary (G : Game V) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, ∃ a b, ∀ w, G.edge v w → w = a ∨ w = b

def ExponentialBinary : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℕ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ global : Bool, ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ G : Game (Fin N), ∃ ι : Fin N → Fin N,
      Binary G ∧ edgeCount G ≤ C * n ∧
      (∀ v, G.priority v ≤ C * n) ∧
      HardInstance G ι (if global then GlobalStep G else LocalStep G) (2 ^ n)

def Wins (G : Game V) (player : Bool) (σ : V → V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  Legal G player σ ∧ ∀ τ, Legal G (!player) τ →
    (if player = false then (playValue G σ τ v).cyclePriority % 2 = 0
      else (playValue G τ σ v).cyclePriority % 2 = 1)

def WinningRegion (G : Game V) (player : Bool) : Set V :=
  {v | ∃ σ, Wins G player σ v}

def IsSinkGame (G : Game V) (ι : V → V) (sink : V) : Prop :=
  WellFormed G ∧ Legal G false ι ∧
    G.edge sink sink ∧ G.priority sink = 1 ∧
    (∀ v, v ≠ sink → 1 < G.priority v) ∧
    (∀ v, Relation.ReflTransGen G.edge v sink) ∧
    ∀ σ, Legal G false σ →
      (∀ v, ValueLE G (value G ι v) (value G σ v)) →
      ∀ v, (value G σ v).cyclePriority = 1

end FriedmannParity
items.natural_language_statement: Finite positional parity games, ultimately periodic plays, three-component valuations, minima over legal counterstrategies, local and global improvement, completed executions, and constrained lower-bound propositions. No witness family or long execution is assumed.
items.readback: The game data are defined on any vertex type $V$; the finite-game constructions below use a finite enumeration of $V$ and decidable equality, and the empty type is included. A game $G$ consists of an owner map $o:V\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, a priority map $p:V\to\mathbb N$, and an arbitrary edge relation. Its well-formedness means that each vertex has an outgoing edge and $p$ is injective. A total map $\sigma:V\to V$ is legal for player $a$ precisely when $G(v,\sigma(v))$ for all $v$ with $o(v)=a$; its values at the other player's vertices are unrestricted. Given arbitrary $\sigma,\tau,v$, play starts at $v$ and iterates the map taking $w$ to $\sigma(w)$ if $o(w)=\mathrm{false}$ and to $\tau(w)$ otherwise. For any sequence $\pi:\mathbb N\to V$, its recurring set is $\{w:\forall t\in\mathbb N,\ \exists k\ge t,\ \pi(k)=w\}$. A valuation is any triple $(p_*,P,L)\in\mathbb N\times\mathcal P_{\rm fin}(V)\times\mathbb N$, without intrinsic consistency constraints. The play valuation first takes $p_*$ to be the supremum of the priorities of recurring vertices, with supremum $0$ on the empty set; it classically chooses a recurring vertex $w_*$ of priority $p_*$ if one exists and otherwise uses the starting vertex $v$, takes $L$ to be the least occurrence time of $w_*$ if there is one and $0$ otherwise, and takes $P=\{\pi(k):k<L,\ p_*<p(\pi(k))\}$, as a set of distinct vertices. Put $\operatorname{rew}(p)=p$ for even $p$ and $-p$ for odd $p$. For finite $A,B\subseteq V$, write $A<_{G}B$ when their symmetric difference has a vertex $w$ such that $p(u)\le p(w)$ for every vertex $u$ of that symmetric difference and either $p(w)$ is even and $w\in B$ or $p(w)$ is odd and $w\in A$; this definition uses an existential maximal vertex and does not assume injectivity unless well-formedness is separately supplied. For valuations $a=(p_a,P_a,L_a)$ and $b=(p_b,P_b,L_b)$, write $a\lhd_G b$ when $\operatorname{rew}(p_a)<\operatorname{rew}(p_b)$, or $p_a=p_b$ and $P_a<_G P_b$, or $p_a=p_b$, $P_a=P_b$, and either $p_a$ is odd with $L_a<L_b$ or $p_a$ is even with $L_b<L_a$; put $a\unlhd_G b$ when $a=b$ as triples or $a\lhd_G b$. A minimum valuation for $(G,\sigma,v)$ is a triple attained by some legal player-$1$ counterstrategy $\tau$ and satisfying $a\unlhd_G\operatorname{val}(G,\sigma,\tau,v)$ for every legal such $\tau$. The value $\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(v)$ is a classically chosen minimum triple if one exists, and $(0,\varnothing,0)$ otherwise. A globally optimal counterstrategy $\tau$ is legal for player $1$ and, for every vertex $v$ and every legal player-$1$ map $\tau'$, has $\operatorname{val}(G,\sigma,\tau,v)\unlhd_G\operatorname{val}(G,\sigma,\tau',v)$. An improving pair $(v,w)$ for $\sigma$ has $o(v)=\mathrm{false}$, an edge $G(v,w)$, and $\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(\sigma(v))\lhd_G\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(w)$; improvability is existence of such a pair. A map $\sigma'$ is allowed from $\sigma$ when it is legal for player $0$ and, at every player-$0$ vertex $v$, $\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(\sigma(v))\unlhd_G\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(\sigma'(v))$. It is an improvement when it is allowed and, if $\sigma$ is improvable, at least one such vertex comparison is strict. A local step is an improvement for which every outgoing successor $w$ of every player-$0$ vertex $v$ satisfies $\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(w)\unlhd_G\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(\sigma'(v))$. A global step is an improvement for which every map $\rho$ allowed from $\sigma$ satisfies $\mathcal V_{G,\rho}(v)\unlhd_G\mathcal V_{G,\sigma'}(v)$ for every vertex $v$. For any proposed step relation and initial map $\iota$, a complete run of natural length $T$ is a total sequence of maps starting at $\iota$, legal for player $0$ at every $t\le T$, both improvable and taking the proposed step at every $t<T$, and not improvable at $T$; nothing is required after $T$. The edge count is the number of ordered vertex pairs satisfying $G$. A hard instance at iteration threshold $K$ consists of a well-formed game, legal initial map, existence of some complete run, and the assertion $K\le T$ for every complete run of every length $T$. The exponential-local assertion is that there is a natural constant $C>0$ such that for every natural $n>0$ there are a natural $N$, a game on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$, and an initial map, with at most $Cn$ edges and every priority at most $Cn$, forming a hard instance at threshold $2^n$ for local steps; exponential-global has the identical quantifiers and bounds with global steps instead. A game is binary when for every vertex $v$ there exist vertices $a,b$ such that each outgoing successor of $v$ is $a$ or $b$, without requiring $a\ne b$ or requiring them to be successors. The exponential-binary assertion chooses one natural $C>0$ before universally quantifying a Boolean $\gamma$ and $n>0$, then chooses $N$, a binary game, and an initial map with the same edge and priority bounds and a hard-instance threshold $2^n$, using global steps when $\gamma$ is true and local steps otherwise. A strategy wins for player $a$ from $v$ when it is legal for that player and every legal opposite-player strategy gives a play valuation of even recurring maximum priority when $a=\mathrm{false}$, using play $(\sigma,\tau)$, or odd recurring maximum priority when $a=\mathrm{true}$, using play $(\tau,\sigma)$; the winning region is the set of vertices admitting such a strategy. Finally, a sink game with initial map $\iota$ and specified vertex $z$ means well-formedness, legality of $\iota$ for player $0$, the edge $G(z,z)$, priority $p(z)=1$, all other priorities strictly greater than $1$, a finite path (including a zero-step path) from every vertex to $z$, and the following universal assertion: every legal player-$0$ map $\sigma$ with $\mathcal V_{G,\iota}(v)\unlhd_G\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(v)$ for all $v$ has recurring-priority component $1$ in $\mathcal V_{G,\sigma}(v)$ for every $v$. All these definitions are total; existence, legality, well-formedness, and consistency of valuations are imposed only where explicitly listed, and statements universally ranging over vertices are vacuous when $V$ is empty.

items.definition_title: Rational primal simplex and cyclic entering-variable selection
items.definition:
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.NonsingularInverse
import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Cast.Order

set_option autoImplicit false

/-! Rational standard-form primal simplex: maximize cᵀx subject to Ax=b, x≥0.
No pivot rule or lower bound is included in the data. The inverse is Mathlib's
total matrix inverse; every permitted basis explicitly has nonzero determinant.
-/
namespace FriedmannSimplex

open scoped BigOperators
open Matrix

structure LP (m n : ℕ) where
  A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℚ
  b : Fin m → ℚ
  c : Fin n → ℚ

abbrev Basis (m n : ℕ) := Fin m → Fin n

def basisMatrix {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n) :
    Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℚ := fun i j => P.A i (B j)

noncomputable def basicValues {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n) :
    Fin m → ℚ := (basisMatrix P B)⁻¹ *ᵥ P.b

noncomputable def basicPoint {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n) :
    Fin n → ℚ := fun j => ∑ i : Fin m, if B i = j then basicValues P B i else 0

def feasible {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (x : Fin n → ℚ) : Prop :=
  P.A *ᵥ x = P.b ∧ ∀ j, 0 ≤ x j

noncomputable def basicFeasible {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective B ∧ (basisMatrix P B).det ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i, 0 ≤ basicValues P B i

def objective {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (x : Fin n → ℚ) : ℚ :=
  ∑ j : Fin n, P.c j * x j

noncomputable def basicObjective {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n) : ℚ :=
  objective P (basicPoint P B)

noncomputable def direction {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n)
    (j : Fin n) : Fin m → ℚ :=
  (basisMatrix P B)⁻¹ *ᵥ (fun i => P.A i j)

noncomputable def reducedCost {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n)
    (j : Fin n) : ℚ :=
  P.c j - ∑ i : Fin m, P.c (B i) * direction P B j i

noncomputable def improving {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n)
    (j : Fin n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, B i ≠ j) ∧ 0 < reducedCost P B j

noncomputable def leaving {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n)
    (j : Fin n) (l : Fin m) : Prop :=
  0 < direction P B j l ∧
    ∀ i, 0 < direction P B j i →
      basicValues P B l / direction P B j l ≤
        basicValues P B i / direction P B j i

noncomputable def pivot {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n)
    (j : Fin n) (B' : Basis m n) : Prop :=
  basicFeasible P B ∧ improving P B j ∧
    ∃ l, leaving P B j l ∧ B' = Function.update B l j ∧ basicFeasible P B'

noncomputable def optimalBasis {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) (B : Basis m n) : Prop :=
  basicFeasible P B ∧ ∀ j, ¬ improving P B j

noncomputable def nondegenerate {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) : Prop :=
  ∀ B, basicFeasible P B → ∀ i, 0 < basicValues P B i

def bounded {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n) : Prop :=
  ∃ R : ℚ, ∀ x, feasible P x → ∀ j, |x j| ≤ R

/-- Distance from the last selected rank. A basic variable cannot enter again,
so including the last rank in the scan agrees with resuming just after it. -/
def cyclicDistance {n : ℕ} (order : Fin n ≃ Fin n) (last j : Fin n) : ℕ :=
  ((order j).val + n - last.val) % n

noncomputable def cunninghamChoice {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n)
    (order : Fin n ≃ Fin n) (B : Basis m n) (last j : Fin n) : Prop :=
  improving P B j ∧ ∀ k, improving P B k →
    cyclicDistance order last j ≤ cyclicDistance order last k

structure State (m n : ℕ) where
  basis : Basis m n
  last : Fin n

noncomputable def cunninghamStep {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n)
    (order : Fin n ≃ Fin n) (s s' : State m n) : Prop :=
  ∃ j, cunninghamChoice P order s.basis s.last j ∧
    pivot P s.basis j s'.basis ∧ s'.last = order j

/-- A finite complete run. The endpoint is genuinely optimal; every edge is an
actual ratio-test simplex pivot. Strictness is a conclusion of source targets. -/
noncomputable def cunninghamRun {m n : ℕ} (P : LP m n)
    (order : Fin n ≃ Fin n) (s : ℕ → State m n) (T : ℕ) : Prop :=
  basicFeasible P (s 0).basis ∧
    (∀ t, t < T → cunninghamStep P order (s t) (s (t + 1))) ∧
    optimalBasis P (s T).basis

end FriedmannSimplex
items.natural_language_statement: Standard-form rational linear programs, actual basic solutions at nonsingular feasible bases, reduced costs, minimum-ratio pivots, and cyclic entering-variable selection. No lower bound is a field or hypothesis.
items.source: Avis and Friedmann, Mathematical Programming2017, §4.1; https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3944
items.readback: For arbitrary natural dimensions $m,q$, a rational LP consists only of $A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times q}$, $b\in\mathbb Q^m$, and $c\in\mathbb Q^q$. A basis label is any map $B:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$; write $A_B(i,l)=A(i,B(l))$, $x_B=A_B^{-1}b$, and $x(B)_j=\sum_{l:B(l)=j}(x_B)_l$, with the total matrix inverse, equal to the zero matrix for a singular square matrix. A point $x\in\mathbb Q^q$ is feasible precisely when $Ax=b$ and all coordinates are nonnegative. The basis is basic feasible precisely when $B$ is injective, $\det A_B\ne0$, and $x_B\ge0$ coordinatewise. The objective is $c^\mathsf Tx$ and the basic objective is $c^\mathsf T x(B)$. For a column $j$ put $d_j=A_B^{-1}A_{\cdot j}$ and $\bar c_j=c_j-\sum_l c_{B(l)}(d_j)_l$; $j$ is improving precisely when it is absent from the image of $B$ and $\bar c_j>0$. A row $l$ may leave for $j$ precisely when $(d_j)_l>0$ and $(x_B)_l/(d_j)_l\le(x_B)_i/(d_j)_i$ for every row $i$ with $(d_j)_i>0$. A pivot from $B$ to $B'$ at $j$ requires $B$ basic feasible and $j$ improving, and requires some such leaving $l$ with $B'$ equal to $B$ with row $l$ replaced by $j$ and $B'$ basic feasible; every ratio-test tie is permitted. An optimal basis here means a basic feasible basis with no improving column, rather than a separately quantified comparison against all feasible objective values. No dimension is assumed positive. The LP is nondegenerate when every basic feasible basis has every coordinate of its basic-value vector strictly positive, and bounded when there is a rational $R$ such that every feasible point $x$ satisfies $|x_j|\le R$ for every column $j$; these universal assertions may be vacuous if there are no such bases or points, and empty dimensions are included. Given a permutation $\omega$ of the $q$ column indices and indices $a,j<q$, define the cyclic distance $\delta_\omega(a,j)=((\omega(j)+q-a)\bmod q)$ using their natural index values and natural subtraction. A Cunningham choice is an improving $j$ with $\delta_\omega(a,j)\le\delta_\omega(a,k)$ for every improving $k$. A Cunningham state consists of a basis label $B$ and an index $a<q$; a step chooses such a $j$, performs the ratio-test pivot just specified, and sets the next stored index equal to $\omega(j)$, not to $j$ unless those indices coincide. A complete Cunningham run of length $T$ is a total sequence of these states with a basic feasible initial basis, a Cunningham step for every natural $t<T$, and an optimal final basis, with no restrictions after $T$. A choice or state requiring an index below $q$ has no instances when $q=0$.

import Definitions.Def_friedmann_simplex
import Definitions.Def_friedmann_parity
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Sort
import Mathlib.Tactic.DeriveFintype

set_option autoImplicit false

/-! The explicit two-centre counter of Disser--Friedmann--Hopp.
Indices here start at zero; the source's level i is represented by i-1.
These definitions contain no lower-bound, progress, or counter-simulation fields.
-/
namespace FriedmannZadeh

open scoped BigOperators Matrix

abbrev Centre (n : ℕ) := {c : Fin n × Fin 2 // c.1.val + c.2.val < n}

inductive Node (n : ℕ) where
  | entry : Fin n → Node n
  | selector : Fin n → Node n
  | cycle : Centre n → Fin 2 → Node n
  | escape : Centre n → Fin 2 → Node n
  | upper : Centre n → Node n
  | centre : Centre n → Node n
  | reward : Centre n → Node n
  | sink : Node n
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

abbrev Strategy (n : ℕ) := Node n → Node n
abbrev Edge (n : ℕ) := Node n × Node n

def entryAt (n i : ℕ) : Node n :=
  if h : i < n then .entry ⟨i,h⟩ else .sink

def selectorAt (n i : ℕ) : Node n :=
  if h : i < n then .selector ⟨i,h⟩ else .sink

def centreAt (n i j : ℕ) : Node n :=
  if h : i < n ∧ j < 2 ∧ i + j < n then
    .centre ⟨(⟨i,h.1⟩,⟨j,h.2.1⟩),h.2.2⟩
  else .sink

def cycleAt (n i j k : ℕ) : Node n :=
  if h : i < n ∧ j < 2 ∧ i + j < n ∧ k < 2 then
    .cycle ⟨(⟨i,h.1⟩,⟨j,h.2.1⟩),h.2.2.1⟩ ⟨k,h.2.2.2⟩
  else .sink

def upperAt (n i j : ℕ) : Node n :=
  if h : i < n ∧ j < 2 ∧ i + j < n then
    .upper ⟨(⟨i,h.1⟩,⟨j,h.2.1⟩),h.2.2⟩
  else .sink

def rewardAt (n i j : ℕ) : Node n :=
  if h : i < n ∧ j < 2 ∧ i + j < n then
    .reward ⟨(⟨i,h.1⟩,⟨j,h.2.1⟩),h.2.2⟩
  else .sink

def owned {n : ℕ} : Node n → Bool
  | .centre _ | .reward _ | .sink => false
  | _ => true

def priority {n : ℕ} : Node n → ℕ
  | .entry _ | .cycle _ _ | .escape _ _ => 3
  | .selector i => 11 + 2 * i.val
  | .upper c => 10 - 2 * c.val.2.val
  | .centre c => 6 - 2 * c.val.2.val
  | .reward c => 12 + 2 * c.val.1.val
  | .sink => 1

def successors {n : ℕ} : Node n → Finset (Node n)
  | .entry i => {.selector i, entryAt n (i.val + 1)}
  | .selector i => if h : i.val + 1 < n then
      {.centre ⟨(i,0),by simp⟩, .centre ⟨(i,1),by simpa using h⟩}
    else {.centre ⟨(i,0),by simp⟩}
  | .cycle c k => {.centre c, .escape c k}
  | .escape _ _ => {entryAt n 1, selectorAt n 0}
  | .upper c => {.reward c, entryAt n 0}
  | .centre c => {.cycle c 0, .cycle c 1, .upper c}
  | .reward c => {if c.val.2.val = 0 then entryAt n (c.val.1.val + 2)
      else selectorAt n (c.val.1.val + 1)}
  | .sink => {.sink}

def legal {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, owned v = true → σ v ∈ successors v

def initial {n : ℕ} : Strategy n
  | .entry i => entryAt n (i.val + 1)
  | .selector i => .centre ⟨(i,0),by simp⟩
  | .cycle c k => .escape c k
  | .escape _ _ => entryAt n 1
  | .upper c => if c.val.2.val = 0 then .reward c else entryAt n 0
  | v => v

def closed {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) (i j : ℕ) : Prop :=
  i < n ∧ j < 2 ∧ i + j < n ∧
  σ (cycleAt n i j 0) = centreAt n i j ∧
  σ (cycleAt n i j 1) = centreAt n i j

noncomputable def bitState {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) : ℕ → Bool := by
  classical
  exact fun i => Nat.rec (motive := fun _ => Bool) false
    (fun k prev => decide (closed σ (n - 1 - k) prev.toNat)) (n - i)

/-- The source's seven successive edge classes, in order of precedence. -/
noncomputable def edgeGroup {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) (e : Edge n) : ℕ :=
  match e.1 with
  | .selector _ => 0
  | .cycle c _ => if e.2 = .centre c then 6 else 1
  | .escape c k => if σ (.cycle c k) = .centre c then 2 else 5
  | .entry _ => 3
  | .upper _ => 4
  | _ => 7

def level {n : ℕ} : Node n → ℕ
  | .entry i | .selector i => i.val
  | .cycle c _ | .escape c _ | .upper c | .centre c | .reward c => c.val.1.val
  | .sink => n

def centreIndex {n : ℕ} : Node n → ℕ
  | .cycle c _ | .escape c _ | .upper c | .centre c | .reward c => c.val.2.val
  | _ => 0

def lastIndex {n : ℕ} : Node n → ℕ
  | .cycle _ k | .escape _ k => k.val
  | _ => 0

/-- Closed, half-open towards a specified vertex, and other centre states.
This is a classification of the current strategy, not an assumed phase. -/
noncomputable def halfopenTo {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) (i j : ℕ)
    (target : Node n) : Prop :=
  ∃ k : Fin 2, σ (cycleAt n i j k.val) = centreAt n i j ∧
    σ (cycleAt n i j (1 - k.val)) ≠ centreAt n i j ∧
    σ (match cycleAt n i j (1 - k.val) with
       | .cycle c l => .escape c l | _ => .sink) = target

inductive Context where | parity | mdp
  deriving DecidableEq

noncomputable def activeIndex {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (bitState σ (i + 1)).toNat

/-- Strict part of the source's within-class ordering. The target parameter is
the direction of the current transition; concrete runs determine it from the
better of b₂ and g₁. Its equivalence to the source phase convention is a target.
-/
noncomputable def internalBefore {n : ℕ} (ctx : Context) (σ : Strategy n)
    (target : Node n) (e f : Edge n) : Prop :=
  let i := level e.1; let k := level f.1
  let j := centreIndex e.1; let l := centreIndex f.1
  let x := lastIndex e.1; let y := lastIndex f.1
  let active := fun a b => b = activeIndex σ a
  let preferred := fun a b => if ctx = .parity then b = 0 else active a b
  match edgeGroup σ e with
  | 4 => k < i
  | 5 => k < i ∨ (i = k ∧ preferred i j ∧ ¬ preferred k l)
  | 2 => k < i ∨ (i = k ∧
      ((closed σ i j ∧ ¬ closed σ k l) ∨
       (¬ closed σ i j ∧ ¬ closed σ k l ∧
         halfopenTo σ i j target ∧ ¬ halfopenTo σ k l target) ∨
       ((closed σ i j ↔ closed σ k l) ∧
        (halfopenTo σ i j target ↔ halfopenTo σ k l target) ∧
        preferred i j ∧ ¬ preferred k l)))
  | 6 =>
      let otherClosed := fun a b c => σ (cycleAt n a b (1 - c)) = centreAt n a b
      (¬ otherClosed i j x ∧ otherClosed k l y) ∨
      ((otherClosed i j x ↔ otherClosed k l y) ∧
        ((bitState σ i = false ∧ bitState σ k = true) ∨
         (bitState σ i = bitState σ k ∧
           (i < k ∨ (i = k ∧
             ((active i j ∧ ¬ active k l) ∨
              ((active i j ↔ active k l) ∧ x < y)))))))
  | _ => False

noncomputable def before {n : ℕ} (ctx : Context) (σ : Strategy n)
    (target : Node n) (e f : Edge n) : Prop :=
  edgeGroup σ e < edgeGroup σ f ∨
    (edgeGroup σ e = edgeGroup σ f ∧ internalBefore ctx σ target e f)

/-- A fixed total ordering of labels completes any ties left unspecified by
the source. Only a linear extension of the source preorder is admitted. -/
noncomputable def linearExtension {n : ℕ} (ctx : Context) (σ : Strategy n)
    (target : Node n) (rank : Edge n → ℕ) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective rank ∧ ∀ e f, before ctx σ target e f → rank e < rank f

/-- A concrete completion of the source preorder. For a strict partial order,
predecessor cardinality increases on every ordered pair; the final label breaks
ties. Hence evaluation requires only polynomially many pair comparisons. -/
noncomputable def sourceRank {n : ℕ} (ctx : Context) (σ : Strategy n)
    (target : Node n) (e : Edge n) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter (fun f => before ctx σ target f e)).card *
    Fintype.card (Edge n) + (Fintype.equivFin (Edge n) e).val

def parityGame (n : ℕ) : FriedmannParity.Game (Node n) where
  owner v := !owned v
  priority := priority
  edge v w := w ∈ successors v

/-- An integer radix realizes lexicographic comparison of priority
multiplicities. This totalizes the source's set comparison for its actual
repeated-priority presentation; equal multiplicities are identified. -/
noncomputable def pgPlayScore {n : ℕ} (σ τ : Strategy n) (v : Node n) : ℤ := by
  classical
  let a := FriedmannParity.playValue (parityGame n) σ τ v
  let M : ℤ := Fintype.card (Node n) + 1
  let W : ℤ := ∑ w ∈ a.path, (-M) ^ priority w
  let H : ℤ := 2 * (Fintype.card (Node n) : ℤ) * M ^ (2 * n + 12) + 1
  let L : ℤ := if a.cyclePriority % 2 = 0 then -(a.length : ℤ) else a.length
  exact (FriedmannParity.reward a.cyclePriority * H + W) * M + L

noncomputable def pgValue {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) (v : Node n) : ℤ := by
  classical
  let scores := (Finset.univ.filter
    (fun τ : Strategy n => FriedmannParity.Legal (parityGame n) true τ)).image
      (fun τ => pgPlayScore σ τ v)
  exact if h : scores.Nonempty then scores.min' h else 0

noncomputable def pgBetter {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) (v w : Node n) : Prop :=
  pgValue σ v < pgValue σ w

noncomputable def pgImproving {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) (e : Edge n) : Prop :=
  owned e.1 = true ∧ e.2 ∈ successors e.1 ∧ pgBetter σ (σ e.1) e.2

noncomputable def pgTarget {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) : Node n :=
  by
    classical
    exact if pgBetter σ (entryAt n 1) (selectorAt n 0)
      then selectorAt n 0 else entryAt n 1

structure CounterState (n : ℕ) where
  strategy : Strategy n
  count : Edge n → ℕ

noncomputable def exceptional {n : ℕ} (improving : Edge n → Prop)
    (count : Edge n → ℕ) : Prop :=
  let e := (entryAt n 0,entryAt n 1)
  let f := (upperAt n 0 1,rewardAt n 0 1)
  count e = 0 ∧ count f = 0 ∧ improving e ∧ improving f

noncomputable def counterRank {n : ℕ} (ctx : Context) (s : CounterState n)
    (target : Node n) (improving : Edge n → Prop) (e : Edge n) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact if exceptional improving s.count ∧ e = (upperAt n 0 1,rewardAt n 0 1)
    then 0 else sourceRank ctx s.strategy target e + 1

noncomputable def counterChoice {n : ℕ} (ctx : Context) (s : CounterState n)
    (target : Node n) (improving : Edge n → Prop) (e : Edge n) : Prop :=
  improving e ∧ (∀ f, improving f → s.count e ≤ s.count f) ∧
    ∀ f, improving f → s.count f = s.count e →
      counterRank ctx s target improving e ≤ counterRank ctx s target improving f

def updateCounter {n : ℕ} (s : CounterState n) (e : Edge n) : CounterState n where
  strategy := Function.update s.strategy e.1 e.2
  count := Function.update s.count e (s.count e + 1)

noncomputable def pgStep {n : ℕ} (s s' : CounterState n) : Prop :=
  ∃ e, counterChoice .parity s (pgTarget s.strategy) (pgImproving s.strategy) e ∧
    s' = updateCounter s e

noncomputable def pgRun {n : ℕ} (s : ℕ → CounterState n) (T : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (s 0).strategy = initial ∧ (∀ e, (s 0).count e = 0) ∧
  (∀ t, t ≤ T → legal (s t).strategy) ∧
  (∀ t, t < T → pgStep (s t) (s (t + 1))) ∧
  ∀ e, ¬ pgImproving (s T).strategy e

/-- Deterministic reward vertices are retained as single-action vertices.
Figure 5 assigns nonzero rewards to g, s, h and zero to the unlabelled vertices.
This avoids discarding the high reward at h when eliminating deterministic
random vertices. -/
def control {n : ℕ} : Node n → Bool
  | .centre _ | .sink => false
  | _ => true

def mdpReward {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) : Node n → ℚ
  | .selector i => (-(N : ℚ)) ^ (11 + 2 * i.val)
  | .upper c => (-(N : ℚ)) ^ (10 - 2 * c.val.2.val)
  | .reward c => (-(N : ℚ)) ^ (12 + 2 * c.val.1.val)
  | _ => 0

noncomputable def transition {n : ℕ} (ε : ℚ) (σ : Strategy n)
    (v w : Node n) : ℚ :=
  match v with
  | .centre c => if w = .upper c then ε
      else if w = .cycle c 0 ∨ w = .cycle c 1 then (1 - ε) / 2 else 0
  | .reward c => if w ∈ successors (.reward c) then 1 else 0
  | .sink => if w = .sink then 1 else 0
  | _ => if σ v = w then 1 else 0

noncomputable def policyMatrix {n : ℕ} (ε : ℚ) (σ : Strategy n) :
    Matrix (Node n) (Node n) ℚ :=
  fun v w => if v = .sink then (if w = .sink then 1 else 0)
    else (if v = w then 1 else 0) - transition ε σ v w

noncomputable def proper {n : ℕ} (ε : ℚ) (σ : Strategy n) : Prop :=
  (policyMatrix ε σ).det ≠ 0

noncomputable def mdpValue {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) (σ : Strategy n) : Node n → ℚ :=
  (policyMatrix ε σ)⁻¹ *ᵥ mdpReward N

noncomputable def mdpImproving {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ)
    (σ : Strategy n) (e : Edge n) : Prop :=
  owned e.1 = true ∧ e.2 ∈ successors e.1 ∧
    mdpValue N ε σ (σ e.1) < mdpValue N ε σ e.2

noncomputable def mdpTarget {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) (σ : Strategy n) : Node n :=
  if mdpValue N ε σ (entryAt n 1) < mdpValue N ε σ (selectorAt n 0)
    then selectorAt n 0 else entryAt n 1

noncomputable def mdpStep {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ)
    (s s' : CounterState n) : Prop :=
  ∃ e, counterChoice .mdp s (mdpTarget N ε s.strategy)
      (mdpImproving N ε s.strategy) e ∧ s' = updateCounter s e

noncomputable def mdpRun {n : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ)
    (s : ℕ → CounterState n) (T : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (s 0).strategy = initial ∧ (∀ e, (s 0).count e = 0) ∧
  (∀ t, t ≤ T → legal (s t).strategy ∧ proper ε (s t).strategy) ∧
  (∀ t, t < T → mdpStep N ε (s t) (s (t + 1))) ∧
  ∀ e, ¬ mdpImproving N ε (s T).strategy e

structure LPState (m n : ℕ) where
  basis : FriedmannSimplex.Basis m n
  count : Fin n → ℕ

noncomputable def leastEntered {m n : ℕ} (P : FriedmannSimplex.LP m n)
    (s : LPState m n) (j : Fin n) : Prop :=
  FriedmannSimplex.improving P s.basis j ∧
    ∀ k, FriedmannSimplex.improving P s.basis k → s.count j ≤ s.count k

noncomputable def lpStep {m n : ℕ} (P : FriedmannSimplex.LP m n)
    (tie : LPState m n → Fin n → ℕ) (s s' : LPState m n) : Prop :=
  ∃ j, leastEntered P s j ∧
    (∀ k, leastEntered P s k → tie s j ≤ tie s k) ∧
    FriedmannSimplex.pivot P s.basis j s'.basis ∧
    s'.count = Function.update s.count j (s.count j + 1)

noncomputable def lpRun {m n : ℕ} (P : FriedmannSimplex.LP m n)
    (tie : LPState m n → Fin n → ℕ) (s : ℕ → LPState m n) (T : ℕ) : Prop :=
  FriedmannSimplex.basicFeasible P (s 0).basis ∧
    (∀ j, (s 0).count j = 0) ∧
    (∀ t, t < T → lpStep P tie (s t) (s (t + 1))) ∧
    FriedmannSimplex.optimalBasis P (s T).basis

abbrev Decision (n : ℕ) := {v : Node n // control v = true}

abbrev Action (n : ℕ) :=
  {e : Edge n // control e.1 = true ∧ e.2 ∈ successors e.1}

noncomputable def rowCount (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Fintype.card (Decision n)
noncomputable def columnCount (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Fintype.card (Action n)

noncomputable def rowAt (n : ℕ) : Fin (rowCount n) ≃ Decision n :=
  (Fintype.equivFin (Decision n)).symm

noncomputable def columnAt (n : ℕ) : Fin (columnCount n) ≃ Action n :=
  (Fintype.equivFin (Action n)).symm

/-- Eliminate a random centre immediately after an action, while retaining all
deterministic reward vertices as single-action decision vertices. Terminal sink
visits have zero continuing occupancy. -/
def afterAction {n : ℕ} (ε : ℚ) (w u : Node n) : ℚ :=
  match w with
  | .centre c => if u = .upper c then ε
      else if u = .cycle c 0 ∨ u = .cycle c 1 then (1 - ε) / 2 else 0
  | .sink => 0
  | _ => if w = u then 1 else 0

/-- Occupancy LP, with one unit of input flow at each nonterminal decision
vertex. Coefficients are generated from the explicit graph and probabilities.
-/
noncomputable def inducedLP (n N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) :
    FriedmannSimplex.LP (rowCount n) (columnCount n) where
  A i j := (if (columnAt n j).val.1 = (rowAt n i).val then 1 else 0) -
    afterAction ε (columnAt n j).val.2 (rowAt n i).val
  b _ := 1
  c j := mdpReward N (columnAt n j).val.1

noncomputable def basisPolicy {n : ℕ}
    (B : FriedmannSimplex.Basis (rowCount n) (columnCount n)) : Strategy n :=
  fun v => if h : ∃ i, (columnAt n (B i)).val.1 = v then
    (columnAt n (B (Classical.choose h))).val.2 else initial v

noncomputable def represents {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n)
    (B : FriedmannSimplex.Basis (rowCount n) (columnCount n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, (columnAt n (B i)).val.1 = (rowAt n i).val ∧
    (columnAt n (B i)).val.2 =
      (match (rowAt n i).val with
        | .reward c => if c.val.2.val = 0 then entryAt n (c.val.1.val + 2)
            else selectorAt n (c.val.1.val + 1)
        | v => σ v)

noncomputable def actionCounts {n : ℕ}
    (s : LPState (rowCount n) (columnCount n)) (e : Edge n) : ℕ :=
  if h : ∃ j, (columnAt n j).val = e then s.count (Classical.choose h) else 0

noncomputable def inducedTie (n N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ)
    (s : LPState (rowCount n) (columnCount n)) (j : Fin (columnCount n)) : ℕ :=
  let σ := basisPolicy s.basis
  let cs : CounterState n := ⟨σ, actionCounts s⟩
  let improving := fun e => ∃ k, (columnAt n k).val = e ∧
    FriedmannSimplex.improving (inducedLP n N ε) s.basis k
  counterRank .mdp cs (mdpTarget N ε σ) improving (columnAt n j).val

noncomputable def InducedSimplexRun (n N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ)
    (s : ℕ → LPState (rowCount n) (columnCount n)) (T : ℕ) : Prop :=
  lpRun (inducedLP n N ε) (inducedTie n N ε) s T ∧ represents initial (s 0).basis

noncomputable def Parameters (n N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) : Prop :=
  0 < n ∧ 7 * n ≤ N ∧ 0 < ε ∧ ε < ((N : ℚ) ^ (2 * n + 11))⁻¹

noncomputable def ParityLowerBound (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∃ T s, pgRun (n := n) s T) ∧ ∀ T s, pgRun (n := n) s T → 2 ^ n ≤ T

noncomputable def MDPLowerBound (n N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) : Prop :=
  (∃ T s, mdpRun (n := n) N ε s T) ∧
    ∀ T s, mdpRun (n := n) N ε s T → 2 ^ n ≤ T

noncomputable def SimplexLowerBound (n N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) : Prop :=
  (∃ T s, InducedSimplexRun n N ε s T) ∧
    ∀ T s, InducedSimplexRun n N ε s T → 2 ^ n ≤ T

noncomputable def Main : Prop :=
  ∀ n N ε, Parameters n N ε →
    ParityLowerBound n ∧ MDPLowerBound n N ε ∧ SimplexLowerBound n N ε

noncomputable def priorityCount {n : ℕ} (S : Finset (Node n)) (p : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (S.filter (fun v => priority v = p)).card

noncomputable def countLT {n : ℕ} (S T : Finset (Node n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, (∀ q, p < q → priorityCount S q = priorityCount T q) ∧
    ((p % 2 = 0 ∧ priorityCount S p < priorityCount T p) ∨
      (p % 2 = 1 ∧ priorityCount T p < priorityCount S p))

noncomputable def countEquivalent {n : ℕ} (S T : Finset (Node n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ p, priorityCount S p = priorityCount T p

noncomputable def countValueLT {n : ℕ}
    (a b : FriedmannParity.Valuation (Node n)) : Prop :=
  FriedmannParity.reward a.cyclePriority < FriedmannParity.reward b.cyclePriority ∨
    (a.cyclePriority = b.cyclePriority ∧ countLT a.path b.path) ∨
    (a.cyclePriority = b.cyclePriority ∧ countEquivalent a.path b.path ∧
      ((a.cyclePriority % 2 = 1 ∧ a.length < b.length) ∨
        (a.cyclePriority % 2 = 0 ∧ b.length < a.length)))

def PgSingleSwitch {n : ℕ} (σ ρ : Strategy n) : Prop :=
  ∃ e, pgImproving σ e ∧ ρ = Function.update σ e.1 e.2

def PgReachable {n : ℕ} (σ : Strategy n) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen PgSingleSwitch initial σ

noncomputable def PgCounterstrategy {n : ℕ} (σ τ : Strategy n) : Prop :=
  FriedmannParity.Legal (parityGame n) true τ ∧
    ∀ v, pgPlayScore σ τ v = pgValue σ v

noncomputable def nextLevel (n b : ℕ) : ℕ := by
  classical
  let S := (Finset.range n).filter (fun i => (b+1).testBit i)
  exact if h : S.Nonempty then S.min' h else 0

noncomputable def Canonical {n : ℕ} (ctx : Context) (b : ℕ)
    (σ : Strategy n) : Prop :=
  b < 2 ^ n ∧ legal σ ∧
  (∀ c k, σ (.escape c k) =
    (if b.testBit 0 then selectorAt n 0 else entryAt n 1)) ∧
  (∀ i : Fin n,
    let j := (b.testBit (i.val+1)).toNat
    if b.testBit i.val then
      σ (.entry i) = .selector i ∧ closed σ i.val j ∧
      ¬ closed σ i.val (1-j) ∧ σ (.selector i) = centreAt n i.val j
    else
      σ (.entry i) = entryAt n (i.val+1) ∧ ¬ closed σ i.val j ∧
      (closed σ i.val (1-j) → σ (.selector i) = centreAt n i.val (1-j)) ∧
      (¬ closed σ i.val 0 → ¬ closed σ i.val 1 →
        σ (.selector i) = centreAt n i.val (if ctx = .parity then 0 else j))) ∧
  (∀ c, σ (.upper c) =
    if c.val.2.val = (b.testBit (c.val.1.val+1)).toNat
      then .reward c else entryAt n 0) ∧
  (b < 2 ^ n - 1 → ∀ c, c.val.1.val = nextLevel n b → ∀ k,
    σ (.cycle c k) ≠ .centre c)

def sourceTarget (n b : ℕ) : Node n :=
  if (b+1).testBit 0 then selectorAt n 0 else entryAt n 1

noncomputable def sourceStep {n : ℕ} (ctx : Context) (b N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ)
    (s s' : CounterState n) : Prop :=
  ∃ e, counterChoice ctx s (sourceTarget n b)
      (if ctx = .parity then pgImproving s.strategy else mdpImproving N ε s.strategy) e ∧
    s' = updateCounter s e

end FriedmannZadeh

/-- Table 1 and the explicit deterministic-vertex occupancy representation. -/
theorem size (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    Fintype.card (Node n) = 16 * n - 6 ∧
    rowCount n = 14 * n - 6 ∧ columnCount n = 26 * n - 12 := by sorry

end FriedmannZadeh

items.theorem_title: Section 5 preserves policy switches and occurrence records
items.natural_language_statement: Every complete MDP run on a permitted construction lifts to a complete run of its generated occupancy LP with exactly the same number of pivots, represented strategy at every step, and count on every action column.
items.source: Disser, Friedmann and Hopp, An exponential lower bound for Zadeh’s pivot rule, Mathematical Programming 199 (2023), 865–936, online 19 July 2022. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-022-01848-x; full version arXiv:1911.01074v2. §5; full version Theorem 6.18 proof. Feasible-basis and ratio-test conditions are in the LP run conclusion.

namespace FriedmannZadeh

/-- Section 5, with every count and every pivot preserved by the occupancy LP. -/
theorem lp_transfer (n N : ℕ) (ε : ℚ) (hp : Parameters n N ε)
    (s : ℕ → CounterState n) (T : ℕ) (hs : mdpRun N ε s T) :
    ∃ z : ℕ → LPState (rowCount n) (columnCount n),
      InducedSimplexRun n N ε z T ∧
      ∀ t, t ≤ T → represents (s t).strategy (z t).basis ∧
        ∀ j, (z t).count j = (s t).count (columnAt n j).val := by sorry

end FriedmannZadeh

milestones.milestone_title: Finite size of the counter and occupancy program
milestones.milestone_description: For every positive n, the graph has 16n−6 vertices and the chosen occupancy representation has 14n−6 rows and 26n−12 columns.

milestones.milestone_title: Priority multiplicities agree with the radix score
milestones.milestone_description: For every positive n, every four strategy functions and every two starting vertices, comparison of their integer play scores is equivalent to the lexicographic cycle-priority, path-priority-multiplicity and length comparison.
Every strategy reachable from the initial strategy by improving single switches has a common legal minimizing opponent strategy whose play from every start eventually remains at the sink.

milestones.milestone_title: Definition 7 ordering has the specified completion
milestones.milestone_description: For each positive n, legal strategy, parity or MDP context, and either possible transition direction, the predecessor-count rank is an injective linear extension of the seven-class source ordering.

milestones.milestone_title: Section 4 probabilities and initial policy are valid
milestones.milestone_description: For every permitted n,N,epsilon, the initial strategy is legal and its normalized Bellman matrix is nonsingular. For every legal strategy, every transition row is nonnegative and sums to one.
For every permitted parameter triple, a complete parity run and a complete MDP run each visit a canonical strategy for every number below 2^n, using their respective canonical conventions.

milestones.milestone_title: Section 5 preserves policy switches and occurrence records
milestones.milestone_description: Every complete MDP run on a permitted construction lifts to a complete run of its generated occupancy LP with exactly the same number of pivots, represented strategy at every step, and count on every action column.
A complete run admits a canonical enumeration in which each selected switch also follows the source’s transition-index convention for the tie rule.
